description:
Consider a communication network made up of several nodes. These nodes are connected by communication links that allow one-way transmission of data from one node to another. Each link between nodes has a specific capacity, meaning it can carry a certain number of bits per second, and there is a cost associated with transmitting data along each link. 
Each node in the network generates data that needs to be sent to another specific node. This data can be sent directly or by passing through several intermediate nodes. Additionally, data from the same origin to the same destination can be split up and sent through different paths.
The goal is to determine the paths that all data should take to reach their intended destinations, while keeping the total transmission cost as low as possible.

NumNodes.definition: Total number of nodes in the network

Capacity.definition: Capacity of the communication link from node i to node j in bits per second

Cost.definition: Cost of transmitting data along the link from node i to node j

SourceDestPairs.definition: Source and destination node indices for each pair

SourceData.definition: Amount of data each source needs to send in bits

objective.description: "Minimize the total transmission cost of sending all data from each source to its corresponding destination through the network"

constraints.description: For each communication link from node i to node j, the sum of data flows of all source-destination pairs on that link must not exceed its capacity

For each source-destination pair k and for each node i, the total outgoing flow minus the total incoming flow must equal: the required data amount for that pair if node i is the source, the negative of the required data amount if node i is the destination, and 0 otherwise (flow conservation with supply/demand)
All data flows on every link for every source-destination pair must be non-negative
